title: Encrypted Messaging Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to maximize privacy and security in encrypted messaging apps like Signal, WhatsApp, and Telegram. Essential privacy hardening tips.
intro: Secure your private communications with this comprehensive privacy hardening checklist for encrypted messaging apps. Learn to properly configure Signal, WhatsApp, Telegram, and other messaging platforms to maximize your privacy protection.

items.task: Use Signal as your primary encrypted messaging app
items.why: Signal offers the strongest end-to-end encryption with minimal metadata collection and open-source transparency.
items.howTo: Download Signal from official app stores only. Verify the developer is Signal Foundation. Enable automatic updates for security patches.

items.why: Fake messaging apps can steal your data and compromise your communications.
items.howTo: Only download from official app stores. Check developer names match official sources. Read recent reviews for security concerns. Verify app signatures when possible.

items.task: Enable app lock with biometric or PIN protection
items.why: Prevents unauthorized access to your messages if someone gains physical access to your device.
items.howTo: Go to app Privacy settings. Enable Screen Lock or App Lock. Choose biometric authentication (fingerprint/face) or strong PIN. Set lock timer to immediate.

items.why: Reduces your digital footprint and limits information available to strangers and potential attackers.
items.howTo: Use initials or nickname instead of full name. Remove or limit profile photo visibility. Hide 'last seen' status, read receipts, and online status from non-contacts.

items.why: Prevents others from finding your account using your phone number, reducing unwanted contact attempts.
items.howTo: In Privacy settings, disable 'Allow others to find me by phone number' or similar options. Turn off contact syncing if not needed.

items.why: Automatically deletes messages after a set time, reducing data retention and potential exposure in device compromises.
items.howTo: Set default disappearing message timer to 1 week or less. Enable for all new conversations. Regularly review and enable for existing chats.

items.task: Verify safety numbers for important contacts
items.why: Confirms you're communicating with the intended person and prevents man-in-the-middle attacks.
items.howTo: Open contact info, tap safety number or encryption keys. Compare numbers in person, via video call, or through another secure channel. Mark as verified.

items.task: Enable sealed sender or similar privacy features
items.why: Hides message sender information from the messaging service, providing additional metadata protection.
items.howTo: In Signal Privacy settings, enable 'Sealed Sender'. For other apps, look for similar metadata protection features in privacy settings.

items.task: Disable cloud backups or use encrypted backups only
items.why: Cloud backups often aren't end-to-end encrypted, potentially exposing your message history to service providers or attackers.
items.howTo: Turn off iCloud/Google Drive backups in app settings. If backups needed, use only encrypted local backups or Signal's encrypted backup feature.

items.task: Regularly audit and remove unnecessary linked devices
items.why: Compromised or forgotten linked devices can provide access to your messages.
items.howTo: Check Linked Devices in settings monthly. Remove any unrecognized devices immediately. Sign out from devices you no longer use regularly.

items.task: Disable read receipts and typing indicators
items.why: Prevents others from knowing when you've read messages or are typing, enhancing your privacy and reducing pressure to respond immediately.
items.howTo: In Privacy settings, turn off read receipts, typing indicators, and online status. Note this is mutual - you won't see others' status either.

items.task: Configure notification privacy to hide message content
items.why: Prevents message previews from appearing on lock screen where others might see them.
items.howTo: In Notifications settings, disable message preview or set to 'Name only'. Configure system notifications to hide sensitive content on lock screen.

items.why: Link previews can leak metadata to websites and may expose your IP address or other identifying information.
items.howTo: In Privacy or Chat settings, disable 'Generate Link Previews' or similar options. Manually preview links using Incognito Browser when needed.

items.why: Protects your IP address during voice calls and prevents direct peer-to-peer connections that could reveal location.
items.howTo: In Signal, enable 'Always Relay Calls' in Privacy settings. For other apps, look for similar IP protection or relay features during calls.
